title: Ethiopian Gurage Chicken
community: Gurage people of central Ethiopia — the hospitality chicken with mekelesha
author: Chef Haile
desc: Gurage Chicken Stew — the Gurage community's Doro Wat, distinguished by the addition of mekelesha (cardamom, rue, and coriander) to the sauce and a final enrichment with ayib. The chicken stew of Ethiopia's most celebrated hospitality tradition.
longDesc: Gurage Doro reflects the same food philosophy as Gurage Kitfo — the mekelesha spice blend brings its characteristic cardamom and rue to the chicken stew, creating a more aromatic version than standard Doro Wat. The ayib added at the very end is the Gurage signature.
ingredients: // Mekelesha: ½ tsp cardamom, ¼ tsp rue, ¼ tsp coriander
2 tbsp ayib (ETH096) — stirred in at the very end
steps: Marinate chicken in lemon and salt 30 minutes.
Add kibbeh and berbere. Toast 4 minutes.
Add mekelesha, garlic, and ginger. Cook 2 minutes.
Add chicken. Add water. Simmer covered 80 minutes.
Off the heat: stir in ayib. Season.
chefTips: The mekelesha goes in with the garlic and ginger — it needs gentle heat, not full toasting.
Ayib is stirred in off the heat — it should not cook.
commonMistakes: Cooking the ayib — it should be stirred in cold.
cookingScience: The ayib (fresh cheese) stirred in at the end is an example of acid dairy enrichment — the lactic acid in the ayib partially denatures any remaining sauce proteins, creating a creamier, more complex texture without the heat that would curdle it if cooked.
reheating: Gently — stir in fresh ayib after reheating.
culturalNote: Gurage Doro is the chicken stew of Ethiopia's most generous hosts — the Gurage people are celebrated throughout Ethiopia for their hospitality, and this chicken stew, with its mekelesha and ayib enrichment, is the expression of that reputation.
